column6: A Docker Compose pilot environment for Ed-Fi API v8 (DMS) PLUS a non-interactive executable acceptance gate. smoke-test.sh runs init/smoke-test.sh in the tools container THROUGH NGINX, so routing and TLS are exercised, not just DMS directly. Its own documented steps: obtain a token, Discovery, a descriptor read, a write and read-back, offset/limit AND cursor paging, a change-query extract, an ETag update plus a stale-ETag 412, a deliberately invalid request, and an assessment-style reference write. One PASS/FAIL/SKIP line per step, non-zero exit on any failure

column1: # ALSO WORTH THE ROW IT DOES NOT GET YET: Ed-Fi-Exchange-OSS/DMS-pilot-testing-kit's README titles
# itself `Ed-Fi-API-v8-pilot-testing-kit` and its OpenSSF badge points at
# Ed-Fi-Exchange-OSS/Ed-Fi-API-v8-pilot-testing-kit. The slug that resolves and the name the
# project calls itself DIFFER — another alias, recorded so no later pass reads them as two repos.
# THE SECOND INSTRUMENT IN THE KIT, which is the part a proposal can actually reuse:
# init/check-edorgs-http.sh (FR-EDORG-14) proves http/edorgs.http's five baseline requests have not
# drifted from bootstrap/baseline-edorgs.json — the single source of truth both the bootstrap and
# the .http file read. Pure text/JSON comparison, NO network, NO token, NO database, runnable
# standalone. That is a fixture-drift gate, and it is the cheapest thing on these shelves to port.
# WHAT LIMB `2` STILL OWNS, and it must be said in a SOW before it is priced: Ed-Fi conformance
# CERTIFICATION is Alliance-administered, not a repository. Vendors publish badges of the form
# "tested against Ed-Fi API Suite 3, V5.3, 6.1, 7.3". An acceptance gate you can run is now
# available; a certificate you can self-issue is not. Those are different procurement facts.
